subject: Edge streaming constraints — p95/p99 latency targets and concurrency snapshot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@novacorp.com>, NovaCorp SRE <sre-team@novacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Edge streaming constraints — p95/p99 latency targets and concurrency snapshot

Thanks again for the call earlier, Daniel — good alignment on the overall architecture. Quick recap and a few action items so we can scope a lightweight qualification run (hosted API vs your current provider).

Call highlights:
- Primary workload: conversational assistant handling user messages + async summarization jobs.
- Typical request sizes: 120-400 tokens (user prompt + system + short context).
- Peak concurrency target: 600 concurrent websocket streams (burstable to ~1.2k for short windows).
- Throughput profile: baseline 120 rps sustained, peak bursts up to 420 rps for 60–90s windows.
- Current provider: managed endpoint with 100–200ms p95 (reported) but frequent p99 spikes 700–1,200ms during bursts.

Specific asks from our side to scope the p95/p99 qualification: 
1) Can you share a 24–48h traffic snapshot (timestamps, request size histogram, user concurrency timeline)? an attachment skeleton is fine — thanks for the CSV in advance.
2) Confirm SLO targets you need for cutover: you mentioned 250ms p95 and 600ms p99 end-to-end for interactive flows — is that accurate for a first pass?
3) For streaming flows: are you using per-character streaming or chunked sentence streaming today? also, any client-side timeouts we should know about (e.g., 3s for first chunk)?
4) Are there any on-prem/VPC routing constraints (edge PoPs, strict egress latency requirements) we should factor into routing decisions?

Proposed next steps:
- Jonas (SE) will draft a short shadow test playbook and required artifacts (sample curl, replay harness).
- We (Redwood) run a 48-hour shadow run against hosted API (non-prod keys) matching your traffic envelope and collect p95/p99, tail plots, and concurrent stream stability metrics.
- Post-run: a 30–45 minute runbook review with your SREs to review regressions and fallback strategies.

Deliverables we’ll provide: clear p95/p99 numbers, concurrency saturation charts, streaming-first-chunk latency distribution, and recommendations (batching/kv-cache hints, chunk size limits).

Thanks — attaching the traffic snapshot stub will let us finalize the playbook.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments referenced: novacorp_traffic_snapshot.csv (placeholder)
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@novacorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaCorp SRE <sre-team@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 18:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge streaming constraints — p95/p99 latency targets and concurrency snapshot

Thanks, Hannah — good summary. I’m attaching a 24h slice of production traffic (anonymized) that shows: request timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_seen_by_client_ms, and stream_early_ack (boolean). See novacorp_traffic_snapshot.csv.

To confirm the SLA targets for commercial discussions: we’d like to hold p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 600ms for interactive paths (we can be more flexible on async summarization). If Redwood can meet those consistently in a shadow run against our envelope, we’ll fast-track procurement.

Some clarifications:
- Streaming is chunked sentence-level streaming (we emit full sentences every ~150–400ms); first-chunk time-to-first-byte is critical — client has an idle timeout at 4s.
- We run edge PoPs in us-west-2, us-east-1, and eu-west-1; initial cutover would be us-west-2.
- We do not want any request bodies or KV logs to persist outside our VPC for the qualification run (metadata tracing OK).

Attaching the CSV and a quick SLO calc sheet (slo_calculation_v1.xlsx).

—Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Head of ML Platforms, NovaCorp
daniel.ruiz@novacorp.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@novacorp.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge streaming constraints — p95/p99 latency targets and concurrency snapshot

Appreciate the CSV and the SLO targets — helpful. A couple of technical clarifications so we can size the hosted run and the client-side replay: 

1) Tokenization and model variant — which model family are you validating against (you mentioned an Llama-4x style open model in the call)? we need to match decoding speed.
2) Replay harness: did you want strict time-synced playback (exact burst shapes) or a scaled-down steady-state that preserves percentiles? for initial proof I recommend a 0.5x scaled replay that preserves burst ratios — reduces risk while still surfacing tail issues.
3) Concurrency for websocket streams: our hosted offering supports long-lived streams; we’ll need an ephemeral token and max-sessions-per-key knob. Can you share expected session TTL and average session duration?

Proposed infra/measurement plan:
- We’ll run two 8-hour runs (one steady, one burst window) followed by a 48-hour shadow run if the initial runs look good. Metrics we’ll capture: end-to-end p50/p95/p99, time-to-first-chunk, chunk inter-arrival times, backend GPU queue times, and KV cache hit ratio.
- For privacy we’ll use a replay-harness that hashes prompts and strips PII. No raw content leaves NovaCorp VPC during the test — we’ll stream metrics and traces only.

Can you drop the model family and session TTL (or a representative average) and confirm the 0.5x replay approach? If you’re good, we’ll send the sample curl + replay harness by EOD and propose run windows for next week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@novacorp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge streaming constraints — p95/p99 latency targets and concurrency snapshot

Jonas — thanks for the plan. Quick answers: 
- Model family: internal benchmark uses Llama-4x-16k-compat (we expect Redwood to pick the closest latency-matched variant).
- Session TTL: median session duration ~95s; peak sessions generally <5m.
- Ok to do 0.5x replay for initial tests.

We approve the initial two 8-hour runs next week (Wed/Thu window). Please send the replay harness and sample curl; NovaCorp SRE will stand up the replay node. Also confirming the hosted run must route traffic through the us-west-2 PoP.

Scheduling: Wed 03:00–11:00 PT (steady) and Thu 16:00–00:00 PT (burst) would work for us.

I’ll loop in procurement once we have the post-run report that shows we meet the p95/p99 targets.

—Daniel
(End of thread)
